title: ANOVA F-Ratio Visualiser
scopeNote: This is the first experiment of the original, the one that builds F out of its two variance estimates. The second experiment on what F cannot carry, the worked-example presets, the browse-then-commit identification task and the select-all interpretation challenge stay in the longer version, and the page says so.
summary: Three groups are drawn from normal populations whose separation, spread and size the learner controls, and a real one-way ANOVA is computed on the generated sample. Separation raises F, within-group spread lowers it, and sample size raises it without the populations changing at all.
learningObjectives: Describe F as one variance estimate divided by another, and say what each estimate is built from.
Explain why F hovers around 1 rather than 0 when the populations are identical.
Distinguish the three separate things that move F, only one of which is the effect.
Explain why F is not a measure of how large a difference is, and what the share of variance adds.
State what a significant F does and does not license the learner to conclude.
interactionTypes: four live controls over the simulated populations
a real one-way ANOVA computed on each generated sample
a strip plot of every simulated person with group means and the reach between them
a seeded redraw that shows sampling variability at fixed settings
a withheld explanation released after the learner has drawn several samples
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted. Every sample is generated and analysed in the browser and is gone when the page is closed.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout, with every control a native range or number input carrying a live value output. The figure carries a description giving the three group means, the settings that produced them, F, its degrees of freedom, p and the share of variance, so no conclusion depends on reading the marks. Group means are marked by a heavy tick rather than by colour, and each row is labelled. The figure scrolls sideways rather than shrinking below legible label sizes on a narrow screen, and becomes a keyboard-reachable region when it does. Every redraw is announced through a polite live region. No timed content and no motion.
dataStatus: Simulated and illustrative. The three groups are drawn from normal populations with means 52 minus s, 52 and 52 plus s and a common within-group standard deviation. Nothing here is a norm, a real dataset or a validated cut-off.
simulationNotes: Randomness is seeded with mulberry32 and Box-Muller normals, so a given seed reproduces a figure exactly. The analysis is a genuine one-way ANOVA on the generated sample rather than a formula displayed from the population values: sums of squares are accumulated from the simulated scores, F is the ratio of the two mean squares, and p is the upper tail of the F distribution on 2 and N minus 3 degrees of freedom, computed from the incomplete beta function. This is why the numbers move when the sample is redrawn at fixed settings, which is the sampling variability the activity wants visible.
readmeTopic: what the F ratio is actually a ratio of, and the three separate things that move it
